headline: First Nations and First Ministers discuss infrastructure, safety and a proposed sovereign wealth fund

sections.label: News
sections.text: On October 26, Prime Minister Mark Carney convened First Nations leaders and provincial and territorial premiers to discuss economic participation, infrastructure and community safety. The federal government announced $260 million over four years for Indigenous workforce readiness, more than $2.5 billion over five years for emergency management and fire protection measures, and more than $630 million over four years to renew and expand First Nations and Inuit policing agreements, alongside proposed ongoing funding. Leaders also discussed potential revenue-sharing arrangements and a First Nations Sovereign Wealth Fund; no established fund was announced.

sections.label: Education and context
sections.text: Community safety, health and Indigenous justice are connected to broader reconciliation priorities. TRC Calls #18 and #19 address health inequities; Call #42 concerns recognition and implementation of Indigenous justice systems. These are contextual connections, not verified changes in Call completion status.

sections.label: Accountability
sections.text: What agreements will be signed, when will funding reach communities, and how will First Nations governments define and measure results? Announcements and proposed reforms must be distinguished from implementation.
